A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DTH testing is an independent predictor of disease progression in HIV-infected patients and may have value in the evaluation and management of patients.
DTH skin test results were an independent prognostic marker in HIV-infected individuals with CD4 counts between 200-500 cells/mm3.
DTH skin testing may be a useful adjunctive test in the evaluation of patients with HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anergy, a lack of delayed-type hypersensitivity (a type of immune reaction) to skin testing, is associated with progression of human immunodeficiencies (HIV) to AIDS.
anergy is a strong predictor of HIV disease, and that it is independent of CD4 cell counts, viral load, and other clinical markers.
DTH skin tests should be performed on HIV-infected patients to determine the risk of progression of disease.
